summary: Tested privacy enforcement + Nano Banana image-generation tool. Backend: 60/60 pytest (13 NEW in test_privacy_and_images.py + 47 regression) pass. Frontend E2E: privacy-badge shows 'Private to you', image-mode toggle switches placeholder to 'Describe the image — Brand Guardian will generate it', optimistic 🎨 user bubble renders instantly, and the generated teal acorn logo is rendered inline in the agent bubble served from /api/files/<hex>.png. TeamPage conv card shows 'Private' badge for direct convs.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1149 lines — splitting suggested in prior iterations is increasingly urgent. The new /generate-image + /files endpoints deserve their own /app/backend/media.py module (image generation + serve_file + ALLOWED_FILENAME_RE together).
ALLOWED_FILENAME_RE includes .pdf but the generator only produces image/* right now — that's fine for forward-compat but unused today; note for future multi-modal (video/pdf) iterations.

generate_image endpoint happy-path persists the user_message BEFORE the LLM call succeeds. If Nano Banana fails, we write a consolation agent error row — good — but the user row is still saved. Consider deferring user_msg insert until after the call, or marking the user_msg with an 'errored' flag, so the transcript doesn't have a prompt with no usable response. Minor — acceptable UX today.

serve_file does find_one({'media_filename': filename}) but there is no uniqueness constraint on media_filename (only a sparse index). A filename collision across conversations is astronomically unlikely given uuid4 but still worth either a UNIQUE sparse index or a positive check that we matched exactly one record before trusting conv access.

Frontend: BACKEND_URL is inlined into every via a template literal — that hard-couples the to the exact backend origin. This works today because CORS allow_origins lists the FRONTEND_URL; cookies are sent cross-origin (SameSite=None presumed). If SameSite is ever tightened, loading will silently break. Consider a same-origin /api prefix proxy for media.

Frontend ConversationPage: privacy-badge logic treats `member_ids.length <= 1` as 'Private'. A group conversation with only the creator (no human invitees, only agents) therefore ALSO shows 'Private to you' — semantically correct but the UI copy might mislead. Consider showing 'Private · Group with agents only' for conv.type === 'group' with 1 member.
TeamPage conv-card badge uses `Shared · ${member_ids.length}` — that count includes the creator, so a 2-person group shows 'Shared · 2' (which reads fine). Just flagging the meaning for future copy.

send() swallows the image failure case into a toast + leaves messages[] containing the agent error bubble injected by the backend — good. Do verify the .filter(m => m.id !== optimistic.id) race doesn't remove the backend's real user_message that has the same prompt (it won't, because IDs differ), but worth a comment.

rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no bugs discovered. All privacy guarantees enforced server-side (list filter, load_conv_or_403 on GET/messages/generate-image), file-serving endpoint correctly checks both filename regex AND conversation membership (returns 400 / 401 / 403 / 404 as specified), image generation works end-to-end with Nano Banana (gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview) — one call produced a 420px teal-acorn logo persisted to /app/backend/uploads/ and rendered inline in the conv. UI affirmations (privacy badges, image-mode toggle, 🎨 prefix) all visible as designed.
